channel.title: GATE Guide — free GATE CSE guides
channel.description: Free guides on the GATE CSE syllabus, weightage, subject topics and preparation, by MD ANISH AHAMAD.

item.title: GATE ECE 2027 Syllabus Changes: Every Word That Moved
item.description: The GATE ECE 2027 syllabus compared word by word with 2026 from the official PDFs. Twelve phrases added, five removed, and the four that change what you study.

item.title: Context-Free Language Questions in GATE CSE: Method and Traps
item.description: How GATE CSE asks context-free language questions. Classify a language fast, use the closure grid, and answer the decidability lists without guessing.

item.title: GATE ECE Subject-Wise Weightage, Counted from Five Papers
item.description: GATE ECE subject wise weightage counted question by question from five EC papers against the official answer keys, with the full table and the section means.

item.title: Normalization Questions in GATE CSE: Keys, 3NF, BCNF
item.description: How GATE CSE asks functional dependency and normalization questions: attribute closure, counting candidate keys, 2NF to BCNF, and lossless decomposition.

item.title: Finite Automata and Regular Language Questions in GATE CSE
item.description: How GATE CSE asks finite automata questions. Counting minimal DFA states, subset construction, regular expression equivalence and the pumping lemma.

item.title: SQL Query Questions in GATE CSE: Patterns and Traps
item.description: How GATE CSE asks SQL query questions. Counting rows on a printed instance, NULL behaviour, GROUP BY and HAVING, NOT IN versus NOT EXISTS and joins.

item.title: CPU Scheduling Questions in GATE CSE: Patterns and Arithmetic
item.description: How GATE CSE asks CPU scheduling questions. FCFS, SJF, SRTF and round robin with context-switch cost, waiting and turnaround arithmetic, and tie rules.

item.title: Pipelining Questions in GATE CSE: Patterns and Traps
item.description: How GATE CSE asks pipelining questions. Cycle time with latches, the split-stage trap, forwarding and stall counting, speedup and CPI, worked out.

item.title: Page Replacement Questions in GATE CSE: FIFO, LRU, Optimal
item.description: How GATE CSE asks page replacement questions. FIFO, LRU and Optimal traces, page-fault counting, Belady anomaly, working sets and demand-paging time.

item.title: Time Complexity Questions in GATE CSE: Reading Code Fast
item.description: How to read loops and code fragments for time complexity in GATE CSE, the asymptotic comparisons that repeat, and the wrong answers built into the options.

item.title: Cache Memory Questions in GATE CSE: Patterns and Arithmetic
item.description: How GATE CSE asks cache memory questions. Tag, index and offset splits, associativity, tag directory size, hit and miss counting and AMAT, worked out.

item.title: Recurrence Relations for GATE CSE: Master Theorem and More
item.description: How to solve recurrence relations for GATE CSE - the three Master theorem cases and their limits, substitution, recursion trees and non-standard forms.

item.title: Linear Algebra Questions in GATE CSE: Eigenvalues to LU
item.description: Linear algebra for GATE CSE by question type - eigenvalue identities, rank and systems of equations, determinant properties, and LU decomposition.

item.title: Probability Questions in GATE CSE: Bayes, Expectation, Traps
item.description: Probability for GATE CSE through the question types that repeat - conditional probability and Bayes, expectation and variance, and the base-rate trap.

item.title: Graph Theory Questions in GATE CSE: Patterns and Formulas
item.description: Graph theory questions in GATE CSE, family by family - degree and edge counting, spanning trees, Euler's formula, colouring, matching and connectivity.

item.title: GATE Virtual Calculator: How to Use It Without Losing Time
item.description: How the GATE on-screen scientific calculator works: key layout, function entry order, memory keys, and the slips that cost CSE candidates minutes.

item.title: How the GATE Score Is Calculated (and Normalised)
item.description: The official GATE score formula and the multi-session normalisation formula from the GATE 2027 brochure, with every symbol defined and one worked example.

item.title: GATE CS vs GATE DA: Which Paper Should You Take?
item.description: GATE CS and GATE DA compared from the official 2027 syllabi - where they overlap, where they diverge, and how the two-paper rule works for a CS candidate.

item.title: GATE CSE 2027 Syllabus PDF: Every Topic, Section by Section
item.description: The official GATE CSE 2027 syllabus PDF link plus every section listed in order, with the marks each subject has carried in recent papers.

item.title: Which GATE CSE Subject to Study First (and Why)
item.description: A dependency-aware order for the ten GATE CSE subjects, built from weightage and difficulty, so every subject arrives after the one it depends on.
